#### Primary literature and attribution

- Évariste Galois, *Sur la théorie des nombres* (1830), read in the 1897 *Œuvres mathématiques* (Gauthier-Villars), pp. 15–19. The construction uses prime characteristic $p$, an irreducible congruence of degree $\nu$, roots of $X^{p^\nu}-X$, primitive roots of order $p^\nu-1$, and successive $p$-powers $x,x^p,\ldots,x^{p^{\nu-1}}$ to obtain the conjugate roots. This is precedent for the source-field orbit and primitive root calculations. The descent of a selected union of orbits, prime-to-$\ell$ projection of multiplicative orders at a second prime, and representation conditions are attributed to A2. [Original text, 1897 edition](https://fr.wikisource.org/wiki/%C5%92uvres_math%C3%A9matiques/5#15)
- Camille Jordan, *Théorèmes sur les groupes primitifs*, J. Math. Pures Appl. (2) 16 (1871), 383–408, p. 383 §1 (and §2 p. 384), together with *Sur la limite de transitivité des groupes non alternés*, Bull. Soc. Math. France 1 (1872–1873), 40–71, pp. 41–43 §1 Théorème I. Jordan (1871) shows that a primitive group of degree $n$ containing a prime $p$-cycle is $(n-p+1)$-transitive and states the alternating-or-symmetric corollary for $n\le3p+1$ (already covering $p+3\le n<2p$ since $p\ge5$); Jordan (1873) proves via Sylow's theorem that for odd prime $p$ and $k>2$ no group of degree $p+k$ not containing $\operatorname{Alt}_n$ is more than $k$-transitive, yielding the unrestricted $n\ge p+3$ range of `JordanPrime`. Transitivity-to-primitivity in $n<2p$, preservation of blocks, the normal-subgroup line-permutation quotient and the nonsolvability application in the stated archive contract are read in A2. [1871 scan](https://www.numdam.org/item/JMPA_1871_2_16__383_0.pdf) · [1873 scan](https://www.numdam.org/item/BSMF_1872-1873__1__40_1.pdf)
- Alpöge's `remark.pdf` p. 1 n. 1 directly identifies the fourteen archive parts. A2 supplies the coordinate, block, root and restriction bodies for the complete algebraic result. The book contributes the exposition, exact examples and counterexamples, and the declaration and consumer map. Because A2 already contains a complete formal statement and proof of this exact criterion, any first-proof priority claim for this textbook route is closed. [Author note](https://alpo.ge/remark.pdf)

**Original literature checked on 2026-11-26.**

- Xia, *Graphical regular representations of (2, p)-generated groups*, arXiv:2304.00541v3, p. 9, Construction 4.1 and Lemma 4.2. The construction proves transitivity for its specific generators, and the block-size argument uses transitivity and an order-$p$ element with $p>n/2$. It specializes to the original theorem. The stronger lower bound on fixed points in Xia's construction belongs to the alternating containment application. [Primary text](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2304.00541v3)
- Jordan (1871), p. 383 §1 and p. 384 §2. Primitivity plus a single cycle of prime degree gives at least $(n-p+1)$-transitivity. Jordan (1873), pp. 41–43, Theorem I adds the odd prime and offset $k>2$ and deduces alternating containment from more than $k$-transitivity. The archive's $p+3\le n<2p$ ensures both $k=n-p>2$ and $p\ge5$. [1871 scan](https://www.numdam.org/item/JMPA_1871_2_16__383_0.pdf) · [1873 scan](https://www.numdam.org/item/BSMF_1872-1873__1__40_1.pdf)

Xia's PDF SHA-256 is `c0f14cc0e3392bda0715192a1324590d400776d519dcdcbaefbcd6ecaafae005`. The Jordan scans are the versions recorded in §4.11.

**Primary literature.** Jordan, *Théorèmes sur les groupes primitifs* (1871), p. 383 §1 and p. 384, Théorème I, supplies the $(n-p+1)$ lift from the primitive group and its cycle. Jordan, *Sur la limite de transitivité des groupes non alternés* (1872–1873), pp. 42–43, Théorème I, uses odd prime $p$, $k>2$ and more than $k$-transitivity in degree $p+k$. Substitution of $k=n-p$ gives the odd-prime case. The elementary graph proof treats $p=2$. Jones, *Primitive permutation groups containing a cycle*, Bull. Aust. Math. Soc. 89 (2014), 202–208, Theorem 1.1 and §3, gives the exact modern statement and its attribution. The scans and preprint were verified online against SHA-256 `da345e365af90ee638e268a6bd0fed4a7c641fb5d78988fd39566a0718c4c9c6`, `40efd3231ebd6b729fff92d7520b60460d04d6538cd66333c8ca44aff77c04c7` and `3c52d1ba707db5106a6d2cf242749e1877e8210f875cf9dd43df8b3b1b9f5c57`, respectively. - **Mathlib community.** At commit `0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474`, Thomas Browning’s Cauchy theorem produces a prime-order element. The fixed-field and restriction steps use the files of Thomas Browning, Patrick Lutz, Yongle Hu, Jingting Wang and Kenny Lau. Johannes Hölzl’s cyclic-group development sends the generator through the quotient. Anne Baanen and Junyan Xu supply the scalar norm and norm transitivity. Riccardo Brasca and Amelia Livingston supply the field Hilbert 90 statement with quotient $u/g(u)$. [Cauchy theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/GroupTheory/Perm/Cycle/Type.lean#L539-L548) · [Fixed fields](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/FieldTheory/Galois/Basic.lean#L415-L435) · [Hilbert 90](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Hilbert90.lean#L127-L159)
- **Classical sources.** Helmut Hasse, *Beweis eines Satzes und Widerlegung einer Vermutung über das allgemeine Normenrestsymbol*, 1931, §1, pp. 64–68, proves the all-degree cyclic theorem by induction from prime degree and credits the Hilbert–Furtwängler antecedent. The original Göttingen issue scan, consulted 2026-11-26, has SHA-256 `9af9af201318ab8aab327db35780b2ea3cb391262daa5cc14731641ef1ca590d`. J. S. Milne, *Fields and Galois Theory* v5.10, Theorem 3.17, Corollary 5.25 and Proposition 5.48, gives the Galois correspondence, Hilbert 90 and norm transitivity. His *Algebraic Number Theory* v3.08, Proposition 7.31 and Propositions 8.1–8.2, gives simple-root lifting and the completion tensor product. His *Class Field Theory* v4.03, VIII Theorem 3.1, gives the classical theorem with the all-place hypothesis. [Hasse’s journal paper](https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/download/pdf/PPN252457811_1931/PPN252457811_1931.pdf#page=69) · [Milne FT](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/FT.pdf) · [Milne ANT](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf) · [Milne CFT](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/CFT.pdf)

**Classical sources.** Hilbert's *Zahlbericht*, §54, Satz 90, reprint pp. 149–150, supplies the norm-one quotient and weighted sum in the cyclic field case. Milne's *Fields and Galois Theory* v5.10, Corollaries 5.15–5.16 and Remark 5.47 supply independence and the separable embedding formulas. Gille and Szamuely, *Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology*, 1st ed., Proposition 4.7.3 and Corollary 4.7.5, pp. 109–111, give the Bockstein cup description and cyclic field norm criterion. Restricting the cyclic characters to the scalar field, the tensor factors have a common cyclic field norm image. The lower character is the upper character multiplied by the top degree, so moving this integer from the character to the scalar gives the power implication. Hasse's separate all-place theorem and its prime-degree antecedents are credited in the tower entry. **Mathlib community.** At commit `0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474`, Jz Pan's linear-disjointness file supplies the coprime-degree and tensor-field criteria. Salvatore Mercuri's valuation comparison, María Inés de Frutos-Fernández's adic equivalences and the completion map in Patrick Massot and Johannes Hölzl's UniformRing file supply the finite scalar square. Kim Morrison and Johan Commelin's tensor maps supply cancellation of the repeated base change. Anne Baanen's norm files give determinant, scalar norm, integer powers and invariance under algebra equivalence. Junyan Xu's norm transitivity joins the two towers. [Linear disjointness](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/FieldTheory/LinearDisjoint.lean#L608) · [Valuation comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/NumberTheory/RamificationInertia/Valuation.lean#L66-L114) · [Tensor maps](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/Maps.lean#L476-L490) · [Norm transitivity](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/RingTheory/Norm/Transitivity.lean#L202-L205)

The Göttingen scan retrieved 2026-11-28 has SHA-256 `9af9af201318ab8aab327db35780b2ea3cb391262daa5cc14731641ef1ca590d`. Milne's *Class Field Theory* v4.03, VIII Theorem 3.1, gives the all-place condition in completion form. His *Algebraic Number Theory* v3.08, Propositions 8.1–8.2 and Corollary 8.4, give the completion factors of the place tensor. The cyclotomic pushout and explicit Bézout witness here follow the archive. Vasilii Nesterov moved the radius results into their current file. ### Chapter 7 normalized Jacquet finite length

- **I. N. Bernstein and A. V. Zelevinsky**, *Induced representations of reductive p-adic groups I*, Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Sup. (4) 10 (1977), 441–472, DOI 10.24033/asens.1333. Sections 1.2 and 1.5–1.9 specify smooth complex representations and the closed-subgroup, modulus, averaging and adjunction conventions. Sections 2.1–2.5 specialize to reductive groups over a non-Archimedean local field, identify the block Levis in GL, and provide cuspidal embedding and the exclusion of quasicuspidal subquotients of proper induction. Sections 2.8 and 2.11–2.14 give finite cuspidal induction, the geometric filtration and length detection by associated Levi Jacquet modules. Numdam scan SHA-256 `8424600228ab72c5937e45edceefcae410a2a0b8f5ebf282185691542aa89092`, checked 26 November 2026. [Original](https://www.numdam.org/item/ASENS_1977_4_10_4_441_0.pdf)
- **A. V. Zelevinsky**, *Induced representations of reductive p-adic groups II. On irreducible representations of GL(n)*, Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Sup. (4) 13 (1980), 165–210, DOI 10.24033/asens.1379. Proposition 1.4 (p. 171) proves preservation of finite length by normalized Jacquet and induction functors in the GL setting. Sections 1.1–1.6 give normalized stages and the row and column calculation, Proposition 1.11 (p. 175) treats the rank-two reducible parameters, §2.3 (p. 177) gives the distinct-cuspidal length used in rank three, and §§9.1–9.2 identify the Steinberg constituent. Numdam scan SHA-256 `663c79f2ee236626385d242d83107410c1a3291ba5584d4b8abee9cf8af428ac`, checked 26 November 2026. [Original](https://www.numdam.org/item/ASENS_1980_4_13_2_165_0.pdf)
- **W. Casselman**, *Introduction to the theory of admissible representations of p-adic reductive groups*, draft dated 1 May 1995. Theorems 3.3.1, 3.3.3 and 3.3.4 distinguish admissibility and its fixed-space lifting from the length calculation. Proposition 5.1.1 and Theorem 5.4.1 give the smooth admissible cuspidal criterion and projectivity and injectivity in the category with one prescribed central character. PDF SHA-256 `78b921fc6331ad2b75389f37d15bd5ac3399e6cfc2d7555e1a4d666e0d42612a`, checked 26 November 2026. [Author's draft](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~cass/research/pdf/p-adic-book.pdf)

The inverse and Gram equations give precisely a separated affine finite-type example over the number field. The two primary topology references were consulted online on 2026-11-26. [Author's text](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/adelictop.pdf)

**Classical sources checked on 2026-11-26.** Assaf Naor and Dan Romik, *Projecting the surface measure of the sphere of* $\ell_p^n$, Ann. I. H. Poincaré Probab. Statist. 39(2) (2003), 241–261, Proposition 1 and Note 1 on p. 244. They give the integrable formula and measure identity for the Minkowski functional with Lebesgue measure and normalized cone measure. The norm unit ball satisfies their body hypotheses. Haar normalization multiplies the radial factor by the same multiple as ambient volume. The first and second factors in this book are the cone measure multiplied by $dc$ and the positive-ray density $r^{d-1}$. Gerald B. Folland, *Real Analysis*, second edition (1999), Theorem 2.49 and (2.50), pp. 78–79, gives the Euclidean product and both nonnegative and integrable forms. ### Chapter 7 lower-derivative positivity

- **Joseph N. Bernstein**, *P-invariant distributions on GL(N) and the classification of unitary representations of GL(N) (non-Archimedean case)*, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1041 (1984), 50–102. Theorem A and §5.3 give mirabolic pairing proportionality. §§7.2–7.4 introduce the shifted derivative and state the classical strict central-exponent condition, with the shell argument in §§9.1–9.4. The scan was retrieved 2026-11-26 (SHA-256 `0522b11a86699ff98627d8da6af48505fc236601775efff97cdb4fb70f0d3eed`). [Original scan](https://www.math.tau.ac.il/~bernstei/Publication_list/publication_texts/Bernstein-P-invar-SLN.pdf)
- **Bernstein–Zelevinsky I and Zelevinsky II.** §§1.8–1.9, 3.5, 4.5 and 4.14 of I give normalized quotients, exactness and the product-derivative filtration. Theorems 1.9 and 4.2 of II give exchange of composition factors and singleton-segment irreducibility for the examples. Original PDFs were retrieved 2026-11-26. [Part I](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.24033/asens.1333/) · [Part II](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.24033/asens.1379/)
- **Alpöge–Claude archive A2.** [§7.4.3.20](../chapters/07-chains-of-theta-lifts.md#74320-from-positive-semidefinite-forms-to-the-strict-lower-derivative-bound) reads `derivPos_of`, the level-form and atom-zero induction, the shell estimate, the eigenvector producer and the scalar normalization at local R3. The chapter gives declaration lines and file hashes. The named atom, splitting, density, lift, derivative admissibility and mirabolic proportionality inputs retain their recorded boundary. [Chapter source map](../chapters/07-chains-of-theta-lifts.md#lower-derivative-form-and-shell-supply)

### Chapter 7 mirabolic derivative finite length and admissibility

[§7.4.3.21](../chapters/07-chains-of-theta-lifts.md#74321-why-mirabolic-derivatives-have-finite-length) follows the direct A2 proof from the ordinary two-block Jacquet module to the twisted right-block quotient and back to the original derivative. The fixed-space induction uses admissible irreducible subquotients of the derivative under its residual group. #### Primary sources and hypothesis attribution

- Bernstein–Zelevinsky 1976, DOI 10.1070/RM1976v031n03ABEH001532, English pp. 44–46 §§5.3–5.4, 5.9–5.10. Section 5.3 fixes a nontrivial additive character over a nonarchimedean local field and recalls local Fourier theory on its additive powers. Section 5.4 identifies the distinguished orbit, with 0 the remaining orbit. Section 5.9 uses smoothness in the form of a nondegenerate action of the convolution algebra. It uses complex coefficients and no admissibility or dimension restriction. Section 5.10 identifies the actual relation span with sections vanishing at its stalk. Thus vanishing in every stated quotient is zero on the same vector. The direct proof here needs only the indexed row family and compact quotient sums. The classical detection result already covers the claimed mathematical theorem. [English original](https://www.uni-muenster.de/imperia/md/content/theoretische_mathematik/topologie/bernstein-zelevinsky.pdf)
- Ibid., 1976, pp. 46–48 §§5.11–5.12, especially 5.12(e). For the smooth mirabolic representation the zero distinguished quotient is equivalent to triviality of the column action. The source uses the short exact sequence of mirabolic functors. The A2 consumer proves the forward implication on each original difference.
- Bernstein–Zelevinsky I, 1977, DOI 10.24033/asens.1333, pp. 444–445 §§1.7–1.9 and pp. 450–453 §§3.1–3.2, 3.5, 3.7–3.8. This supplies the relation quotient convention with half modulus and the normalized highest-derivative pairing. A2 uses bare actions here. The ordinary final step has determinant-one unipotents and no change of exponent. The prior conductor result treats the twisted step at its already specified scope. [Original](https://www.numdam.org/item/ASENS_1977_4_10_4_441_0.pdf)
- The LUMI guide provides context for partial local Langlands on its restricted classes. The compact-cover and finite-sum proof is credited to the A2 authors. The explanatory development and exact examples are editorial. [Community source, §Partial local Langlands](https://github.com/aapolipponen/rh-lean-check-lumi/blob/c6d0e2bc06ae4562d6656c6ef118739670d19eeb/docs/05-galois-representations.md#L37)

- Retrieved 2026-11-26, `bz1976.pdf`, SHA-256 `72dc22eb9991112936a88327f00d0f02a16a2bf8747518ca0ecfeeadd188e50c`.

**Primary sources.** Harish-Chandra, §37 and Theorem 16, and Atiyah–Schmid, (8.1) and its proof through p. 47, give the same numerical root quotient under one Haar measure. Atiyah–Schmid (8.8)–(8.19) and Zuckerman, *Appendix on tensor products*, Theorem A.1, give the finite-dimensional and dual translation comparison. Gould's characteristic matrix projectors (7) and trace formulas on p. 408 give the two algebraic partial-trace factors for distinct roots, with the archive's defining and dual operators obtained by negating the barred and unbarred matrices. Classical attribution comes from F. Bruhat, with notes by Sunder Lal, TIFR 1963, Part I Ch. 1 §7, Theorem 3 (nontrivial valuation of arbitrary ordered-group rank in its own topology), Andrew V. Sutherland's Lecture 1 pp. 4–5 (order and uniformizers in the DVR) and Lecture 10 Theorem 10.4 and Remark 10.7 (finite extension of a complete DVR's norm), and J. S. Milne's §7 note 2 and Lemma 8.6 (Haar dilation and the two real normalizations). The older Lean formalization by María Inés de Frutos-Fernández and Filippo Alberto Edoardo Nuccio Mortarino Majno di Capriglio covers the discrete-valuation and DVR interface in CPP 2024, §§2.2–2.3. The Frobenius-norm result is in [A2](#1-the-lean-archive-primary-source), SHA-256 `9631b4f020199e580ba86178cb56c6e9b09f690c2369a80dc4334aa93f49c7fc`, with Lean `v4.33.1` and Mathlib `0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474`. - **Classical sources.** Costin's Proposition 1.0.3 and Lemma 1.1.1 give the von Neumann inverse, the forward series identity on the open unit ball and commuting addition. Lawson §2.5 and Theorem 20 give the local matrix logarithm and matrix-group coordinates. Higham, D. S. Mackey, N. Mackey and Tisseur §2 give the sesquilinear adjoint, its product reversal and the form-automorphism inverse. Higham and Lin §3.1.6 use the spectral condition excluding the closed negative real axis for the principal logarithm. Loring §1 gives skew-Hermitian logarithms for ordinary unitary matrices via an angular branch. Sources checked 2026-11-28. [Costin](https://math.osu.edu/~costin.9/7212-2020/FA1.pdf) · [Lawson](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~lawson/liecontrol.pdf) · [Higham–Mackey–Mackey–Tisseur](https://eprints.maths.manchester.ac.uk/47/2/paper.pdf) · [Higham–Lin](https://eprints.maths.manchester.ac.uk/2067/) · [Loring, v4](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.6151v4)

Invertibility of $n$ in $E$ permits the natural separable-closure Kummer sequence and includes mixed characteristic with residue characteristic dividing $n$. **Hypothesis attribution.** Bloch and Kato's (3.7.2)–(3.7.3) give the same-characteristic crystalline kernel and its integral inverse image. Their Proposition 3.8 gives the integral–divisible $f/f$ annihilators for a continuous finite-rank lattice with de Rham rational representation and its cyclotomic dual. Rubin's Theorem 1.4.1 gives the classical local Tate pairings and their coefficient targets. His Remark 1.3.6 extends the image and inverse-image conventions of Definition 1.3.4 to $p$. Lemma 1.3.8(i) identifies the finite-torsion condition with the image from the corresponding integral lattice for each nonzero level parameter. Proposition 1.4.3(c)(i)–(ii) assumes the selected rational subspaces are already exact orthogonal complements at $p$. These results give the classical comparison. The abstract datum's `IntegralDuality` and the comparison with classical period/cohomology objects remain named arithmetic inputs. Cohomology classes become exact cocycle representatives through Lemma 10.13ej. The same-carrier transport and four test implications are the A2 constructions read in §10.4.7.12. [Bloch–Kato, pp. 353–354, fetched 2026-11-28, SHA-256 ec89c6436c7e16580791eddd562c8c04a12442d8a8484f8ac75c5ea8dc04f5e5](https://virtualmath1.stanford.edu/~conrad/BSDseminar/refs/BKTamagawa.pdf) · [Rubin, pp. 14–19, fetched 2026-11-28, SHA-256 1b0229731e38bfaaa55b38a219c055019d1c7db1f0ecec3c083125da87b6e8e4](https://wstein.org/people/rubin/book/hEulerSystems.pdf)

**Bridge hypotheses.** At each $v\mid\ell$, `bkP.br i v hv` fixes the coefficient embedding `Bw.toLL.toAlgebra`, the group isomorphism and the matching local cyclotomic character. The projection `(h.1.2.1 v hv (Tgl i s) (Or.inr rfl)).1` gives `IsdRW`, hence `IsDR` on the original representation. The projection `(h.2.2.2.2.2.1 (X.l i) Bw.Kw).2.2` gives `bkBCore` in `Gen.adm3`. `GoodO` and the full right dual lattice are checked on that coefficient ring. For §10.4.7.12 the inverse different comes from `GoodO` and the identification of the coefficient ring with the integral closure via `PowerImageOpen.main`. The original-side `IsDR`, the cyclotomic lattice and both lattice duality implications are hypotheses of the base test. The deeper production of the period comparison, the remaining `GalHyp` fields, `bkACore`, `LocalTateDualityK`, `h2_inj` and finite Part C retain their own interfaces.

**Intervening manuscripts.** The contributors' Chapter 10 manuscripts §10.4.7.7 (the `ChooseH` corank witness), §10.4.7.8 (`SpanTwo`), §10.4.7.9 (`SpanOdd`) and §10.4.7.10 (`EqDim`) give the context for these calls. Their A2 loci are IE/`ExistsElementsSelmerFormsSmallCorank.lean`, IE/`SpanTwoOfGaloisHypothesis.lean`, IE/`CocycleFormsSpanOddResidueChar.lean`, and IE/`ResidualSelmerFinrankEqDual.lean`. The `EqDim` manuscript is the reference for the global count. Local use of the two arrows here takes place before that count. [Archive A2](#a2)

**Evidence.** The displayed production proofs have local R3 source readings and independently reviewed conditional expositions. The exact finite models are `[Expository]` examples. Kernel replay, compiled `Main` reachability and peer review are separate questions. Frontier K §§1.3–1.8 supplies the community twist-and-frame map and its discussion of dependency scope. ### Chapter 2 Hölder and Bochner products

- **Historical source.** Frigyes Riesz, *Untersuchungen über Systeme integrierbarer Funktionen*, *Mathematische Annalen* **69** (1910), 449–497. The journal scan was retrieved again on 2026-11-28, SHA-256 `b91fcc78d55c02a64dca4e42f9cb030e52e7cb42d20a848915d5e40bda4ba372`. Printed p. 455, (1), gives the finite-sum bound for $p>1$ and its conjugate. Printed p. 456, (5), supplies the integral comparison on Riesz's domain, with existence of the right-hand integrals supplying existence on the left. The p. 455 footnote gives “p. 95” for Minkowski's finite-sum triangle inequality (2). The cited printed page treats three-dimensional lattices. Riesz derives the integral triangle inequality separately as (6) on p. 456. The precise original location of the finite-sum inequality remains open. [Riesz, pp. 455–456](https://real.mtak.hu/214052/1/Riesz_14_Math_Annalen_1910_449-497.pdf#page=7) · [Minkowski, printed p. 95](https://archive.org/details/diophantischeapp00minkuoft/page/n108/mode/1up)
- **Mathlib.** The finite real conjugacy, scalar Young and weighted AM–GM connect to the normalization and extended-moment branches at `MeasureTheory/Integral/MeanInequalities.lean:66–166`, the two-weight, finite-family and distinguished-factor declarations at :168–261, and the separate real-exponent change of powers at :277–308. The endpoint size uses `MeasureTheory/Function/EssSup.lean:348–362`. At `MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/CompareExp.lean:32–51,166–272,282–327`, the first use of the real-exponent lemma compares exponents using the constant one and the second estimates the size of a pointwise operation. Multiplication membership and the exponent-one equivalence yield `MemLp.integrable_mul`. All files here are at the Mathlib pin in A2's manifest, line 10. [Real conjugacy](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Data/Real/ConjExponents.lean#L48-L62) · [Scalar inequalities](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Analysis/MeanInequalities.lean#L130-L150) · [Integral inequalities](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/MeanInequalities.lean#L66-L308) · [Exponent dispatch and membership](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/CompareExp.lean#L166-L327) · [Bochner bridge](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/L1Space/Integrable.lean#L1085-L1088)
- **Archive A2.** `src/Formalism/FlagUnipotentLattices/MinkowskiFactorialBounds/BlockMinorSumCounterexample.lean:749–807,882–908` uses the equal-share case for the moments of ratio products. `src/Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/IntegralCasts/CapelliIdentities/ConvSqLe.lean:7–37` uses two half weights on volume. `src/Development/AutomorphicSpectrum/Proofs/BlockDecomposition/L2InnerDerivativeTranslate.lean:52–85,89–105` uses the $(2,2,1)$ input-first triple for the uniform section bound and the two Bochner subtraction premises on the same quotient measure. [A2, pinned archive](#a2)
- **Companion sections.** The dense extension supplies the Bochner $L^1$ construction. Riesz–Fischer handles $1\le p\le\infty$ with complete target and uses the integral Minkowski estimate. [Dense extension](../chapters/02-functional-equations-and-primitive-characters.md#banach-dense-extension) · [Riesz–Fischer](../chapters/02-functional-equations-and-primitive-characters.md#lp-riesz-fischer-completeness) · [Integral Minkowski](../chapters/02-functional-equations-and-primitive-characters.md#integral-minkowski-supply)

### Chapter 1 §1.2.2.8, Hilbert expansion

**Community formalization.** Heather Macbeth is credited in the header of the pinned Hilbert-sum and Hilbert-basis source. The edition follows the archive manifest pin 0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474. [Mathlib l2Space.lean](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/l2Space.lean)

**Classical reference.** NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §1.8(i), Parseval's Formula, consulted 2026-11-25 for the circle precedent. [DLMF](https://dlmf.nist.gov/1.8#Px2)

**Book exposition.** [§1.2.2.8](../chapters/01-statement-and-fidelity.md#1228-hilbert-expansion-and-the-norm-behind-poisson-summation) proves the conditional expansion theorem and follows its use from norm convergence to the separate Poisson evaluation step.

The compact model uses the Iwasawa and modulus inputs in §7.4.3.10. Casselman (1 May 1995 draft, retrieved 2026-11-28), Theorem 2.4.2 and Propositions 3.1.1–3.1.4, gives the unimodular pairing and normalized unitary induction for smooth coefficients. The archive reads the extended nonnegative two-fiber formula. PDF SHA-256 `78b921fc6331ad2b75389f37d15bd5ac3399e6cfc2d7555e1a4d666e0d42612a`. **Primary literature.** Hazewinkel 1978 §2, pp. 8–16 and §4 (4.1.2), p. 20 give functional-equation integrality and prime binomial background for the height-two log. The functional equation applies to the height-two law over $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$ with ideal $p\mathbb Z_{(p)}$, base $q=p^2$, identity endomorphism and leading coefficient one. Hazewinkel §2.3.4, p. 11 also gives Dwork's one-variable quotient criterion over the completed maximal unramified extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, with the arithmetic Frobenius on coefficients. Its integral-coefficient congruence modulo $p$ is the scalar hypothesis of §8.4.22, and the formal logarithm of a constant-one series gives its zero-constant phase. The two-variable comparison and the precise odd-log coboundary consumer follow A2. Serre 1960 §3 p. 419 gives the two-variable quotient criterion with rational coefficients and constant one, specializing the finite-variable criterion to `Q_p` with the identity coefficient lift. Serre credits Dwork 1958, Lemma 1. Dwork 1962 §4(a), p. 56, (4.3)–(4.4) gives the one-variable Artin–Hasse exponential and its integrality at the usual $p$-adic normalization. Hazewinkel 1978, Chapter I, §1.6, (1.6.1), p. 5, and (1.6.8), p. 7, gives logarithmic recovery and the p-typical recurrence. Lemma 2.2 and §§2.3–2.4, pp. 9–15, give substitution stability and inverse integrality under the ideal and Frobenius hypotheses. **Lubin–Tate source [Paper].** Jonathan Lubin and John Tate, *Formal Complex Multiplication in Local Fields*, Ann. of Math. 81 (1965), pp. 380–387. Lemma 1, p. 381 and its Remarks on p. 382 give the homogeneous correction and uniqueness, and Theorem 1, p. 382 gives the formal operations. Their prime element and finite residue cardinality ensure the quotient Frobenius assumptions. Theorem 2 starts on p. 383 and uses Eisenstein on p. 384. The general polynomial norm equality in the book uses the elementary comparison of terms at the same absolute value and the exact iteration hypothesis. ### Chapter 2 Möbius inverse and multiplication fibers

The two proofs concern the strict branch for complex Dirichlet characters of every positive modulus. The branch uses series agreement for $\Re s>1$ and the convolution identity. The absolute convergence failure on $\Re s=1$ marks the boundary of this argument. [§2.6.3](../chapters/02-functional-equations-and-primitive-characters.md#263-the-möbius-inverse-on-the-open-half-plane) · [§2.6.3.1](../chapters/02-functional-equations-and-primitive-characters.md#2631-regrouping-an-absolutely-convergent-product-by-multiplication)

- **Pinned sources.** A2 SHA-256 `9631b4f020199e580ba86178cb56c6e9b09f690c2369a80dc4334aa93f49c7fc`; its manifest pins Mathlib `0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474`. In the strict branch, `LFunction_eq_LSeries` transports `LSeries_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re`, which consumes `LSeries.mul_mu_eq_one`. The latter uses two summability witnesses, `LSeries_convolution'`, `convolution_mul_moebius` and `LSeries_delta`. The product comes from `LSeriesHasSum.convolution` through `summable_mul_of_summable_norm`, `HasSum.mul`, `HasSum.tsum_fiberwise` and `term_convolution'`. [A2](#a2) · [Strict branch](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Nonvanishing.lean#L398-L401) · [Consumer](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Dirichlet.lean#L209-L232) · [Fiber formula and product](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Convolution.lean#L101-L154)
- **Classical context** (accessed 2026-11-28). DLMF (27.5.1)–(27.5.2) supply the coefficient convolution and Möbius divisor identity. DLMF (25.15.1) uses $\Re s>1$, (25.15.3) uses the nonzero residues at modulus greater than one, and (25.15.4) gives the factors removed on change of level. Lebl’s Proposition 2.6.3 covers rearrangement of absolutely convergent real series. His Theorem 2.6.5 is Mertens’ theorem for the additive Cauchy product of two convergent series, with one absolutely convergent. Tao’s Remark 37 identifies Tonelli for sums with the counting-measure case; Corollary 46 gives Fubini–Tonelli. The book’s transport proof here works directly with complex finite sums and finite absolute mass. Euler’s prime reciprocal divergence enters by name for the boundary comparison. [DLMF §27.5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.5) · [DLMF §25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15) · [Lebl, *Basic Analysis I*, §2.6](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_moreonseries.html) · [Tao, *245A Notes 6*](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2010/10/30/245a-notes-6-outer-measures-pre-measures-and-product-measures/) · [Prime reciprocal divergence](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/NumberTheory/SumPrimeReciprocals.lean#L98)

The detailed multiplication-fiber manuscript received an independent-source review (2026-11-24, five claims sustained, with the Tao citation corrected to Remark 37). The joined archive SHA-256 is 9631b4f020199e580ba86178cb56c6e9b09f690c2369a80dc4334aa93f49c7fc. [A2 provenance](#a2)

The source chain starts at Main.lean:4, through MainTheorems.lean:7–9, MainConclusion.lean:7–11 and the open-parameter handoff in ThirdPlaceSeries/SiegelEisensteinSecondTermHypotheses.lean:44–73 and OpenOrbitOfUnramifiedExponents.lean:50–53,69. The tied degree comparison in Proofs/FlagMeasures/FormalDegreeRatioEqVandermondeRatioAlongLine.lean:65–109,140–174 enters the row estimate at Proofs/DecoratedLatticeProofs/RowAmplitudeBoundsUniformSingletonWidth.lean:104,119–120. ### Chapter 8, §8.4.4 — Finite jets

Use the A2 declaration paths at the section’s source map and A2-pinned Mathlib where marked. Katz (1976), doi:10.2307/1970966, is the cited historical comparison. The LUMI guide charts the jet bound and later accumulation. [Katz](https://doi.org/10.2307/1970966) · [G1](#g1)


<a id="sources-ch11-sinnott-stickelberger"></a>

### Chapter 11, §§11.4.3.1–2 — Sinnott and Stickelberger

A2 records the difference and nonvanishing producers and the ideal-membership-to-rank argument. William Sinnott (1984) gives the rational-function method, Bruce Ferrero and Lawrence C. Washington (1979), doi:10.2307/1971116, give the classical result, and Washington (1997), §§6.2, 10.2 and 16.2 gives the cited Stickelberger, reflection and transform context. [Ferrero–Washington](https://doi.org/10.2307/1971116) · [Washington](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-1934-7)

#### Classical sources [Paper]

PDFs retrieved from the linked originals on 2026-11-28. The hypotheses in each entry identify the specialization or context used in the chapter.

| Source | Hypotheses and use |
|---|---|
| Fontaine, Représentations p-adiques semi-stables, Exposé III, §§1.4.1–3, pp. 122–123, §1.5.2 p. 124 | G-R1 asks for a nonzero reduced ring, G-R2 assumes comparison injectivity for all representations, and G-R3 requires a unit on each nonzero stable scalar line. The full-rank proof uses injectivity before computing the determinant character. Fontaine's two field letters distinguish the invariant field from the representation base. [Original](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__223__113_0.pdf) |
| Brinon–Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, Definition 5.1.1 and Examples 5.1.2–3, pp. 66–67, Theorem 5.2.1(1), pp. 68–70, parts (2)–(3), pp. 70–72 | An F-algebra domain with group action and fixed field is the setup. Domain and fixed fractions prove the rank bound and comparison injection by a minimal relation. Stable-line unithood gives full-rank comparison through the top exterior power. The Hodge–Tate Laurent example and the de Rham valuation-ring nonunit motivate the two rational models. |
| Brinon–Conrad, Theorem 9.2.10 and Proposition 9.2.11, pp. 143–144, Lemma 9.2.12, p. 145 | Logarithm choice and scalar-extended embedding, semistable regularity, and the crystalline inclusion with monodromy zero are context. The A2 potentially fixed U-space uses a finite compositum and the constant-polynomial tensor inclusion. [Original](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf) |
| Fontaine, Le corps des périodes p-adiques, Exposé II, Théorème 4.2.4, pp. 86–87, proof §4.3, pp. 87–89 | The semistable-to-de Rham scalar-extended ring embedding uses a choice of logarithm. The crystalline consumer in §6.4.24 uses the elementary constant-polynomial map. [Original](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__223__59_0.pdf) |
| Keith Conrad, Galois Descent, Definition 2.1 p. 2, Example 2.6 p. 3, Theorem 2.14 pp. 4–6 | A finite Galois extension and a genuine group structure give a full fixed form by scalar extension. The coordinate lemma in §6.4.26 tests uniqueness on an already fixed independent family, even for a single additive semilinear operator. [Original](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/galoistheory/galoisdescent.pdf) |
| Milne, Fields and Galois Theory v5.10, Proposition 7.12(a) p. 97, Theorem 7.13(c) p. 98 | The characteristic-zero algebraic closure is Galois over the base. An intermediate field is the fixed field of its fixing subgroup and conjugation transports that subgroup. Intersect with the preserved U to obtain the field of the coordinate count. [Original](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/FT.pdf) |

**Classical precedents.** J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Number Theory*, v3.08, printed p. 31, gives the finite-free multiplication determinant and its multiplicativity. The Stacks Project, Lemma 31.18.6, constructs the determinant norm by choosing bases locally in positive degree. The book supplies the elementary adjugate argument, its evaluation at the identity and the explicit examples. Originals consulted online on 2026-11-28. **Prior work.** Jürgen Pöschel, *On the Siegel–Sternberg linearization theorem*, arXiv:1702.03691v2, §5, Theorem 5.2, p. 16 (PDF SHA-256 `ff82bcacbee575e86c1a86381fc9ec7d2e344fff2070a54141549e2a59e562c4`). The implication (i) to (iii) starts with a local diffeomorphism in the weighted differentiability class $E^m$ and an fdb weight. After normalization at a fixed point and shrinking for a small derivative seminorm, it obtains a bound uniform in the cutoff of the derivative of the inverse correction. Gouëzel credits this finite-cutoff technique at [Inverse.lean:342–359](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Analysis/Analytic/Inverse.lean#L342-L359). The general normed-field hypotheses and the partial-sum inequalities used here come from the Mathlib declarations in the table. [Pöschel, §5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1702.03691#page=16)

### Chapter 12 regular local rings and principal dimension drop

[Textbook §12.4.4](../chapters/12-galois-representations-and-local-langlands.md#why-a-regular-local-ring-is-a-domain) follows the proof by induction on the maximal-ideal generator number. The quotient lemma replaces one cotangent basis element and applies the two height bounds. The induction chooses a parameter outside the finitely many minimal primes, obtains primality of its principal ideal from the quotient, and uses Nakayama to kill a minimal prime inside it.

**Archive.** [A2](#a2) SHA-256 `9631b4f020199e580ba86178cb56c6e9b09f690c2369a80dc4334aa93f49c7fc`. ## Chapter 14 Fourier convolution and the reflected Mellin multiplier

[Textbook §14.4.2.7](../chapters/14-masullos-trace-formula-route.md#fourier-convolution-and-the-reflected-mellin-multiplier) uses the two-integrable-input Fourier convolution theorem, then the reflected kernel and the $L^2$ extension. [§14.4.2.6](../chapters/14-masullos-trace-formula-route.md#mellinplancherel-on-the-positive-multiplicative-group) develops the inherited logarithmic Haar coordinates and Plancherel input. [Declaration map with consumers and read levels](../notes/proof-map.md#chapter-14-convolution-and-representatives)

**Classical source.** NIST DLMF §1.14(i), (1.14.1) and (1.14.5), checked online 2026-11-28, gives the scalar convolution theorem with two absolutely integrable inputs. Its forward phase is $e^{ixt}$ and each symmetric normalization uses $(2\pi)^{-1/2}$. The positive-power Mellin convention comes from Masullo (D.3.2.2) and §4.4.1, pp. 189–190. The Gaussian and Schwartz periodization inputs are treated in Chapter 1. The textbook’s Banach-valued real-line specialization, norm estimates and examples are exposition of these classical and pinned results. [DLMF §1.14(i)](https://dlmf.nist.gov/1.14#Px2) · [Masullo](https://math216.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/the-music-of-the-primes.pdf#page=802) · [Chapter 1 §1.2.2.7](../chapters/01-statement-and-fidelity.md#1227-from-poisson-summation-to-theta-inversion)

### Declaration attribution

- **Moritz Doll** introduced the Fourier convolution declarations and the $L^2$ Fourier equivalence. The pinned convolution proof incorporates the removal of continuity hypotheses by Dennj. Doll also introduced `LinearEquiv.extendOfIsometry`. [Fourier convolution](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/7d812d63488c4c350625b66aeb4e3528bb9d7fbd) · [Weakened hypotheses](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/07f4b8dcd071cb3a38a57d99a505ec56667c6be4) · [Plancherel](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/a10b7544deddadbdc1d4ca750810bbf11ae7e0f1) · [Isometric extension](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/a4819b5c820bcc1e2bf3de3efee6c84f5fef44d8)
- **Floris van Doorn** introduced the convolution integrand, a.e. existence, $L^1$ output and flip declarations. The Lean 4 port of his product integration file by Ruben Van de Velde supplies Fubini and its swap, with later weakening of hypotheses by Yury G. Kudryashov. [Integrand](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib3/commit/a07493af5f1c372f3f5dfb79f53b34944db2ef4f) · [Convolution](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib3/commit/41ca601555ef8a6e4c241fff820f8a00531e27b2) · [Fubini port](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/892102cacacea1891583b58484d60fc8b98246c4) · [Product assumptions](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/7dffcc4b8cf7f65cdda6024e5c5531ee3de9eb7a)
- **Yury G. Kudryashov** introduced the continuous family of measure-preserving compositions. **Rémy Degenne** introduced the indicator-inner-product and sigma-finite set-integral uniqueness declarations. [Composition continuity](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/966a472f11ccaf49e93aad12905519f5a21a8459) · [Indicator test](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib3/commit/f302c979512cbceca287296035019909a53260b7) · [Uniqueness](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib3/commit/608faf0ae4c6798b1f27fa32596e0b4fd88dc7f3)
- **Sébastien Gouëzel** introduced the continuous-linear-map lift `compLpL` over the reals. **Rémy Degenne** extended it to the real-or-complex setting, and **Moritz Doll** supplied the semilinear form at the pin. [Original lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib3/commit/49e50ee5c981802cd493d2e63b5f93750951872c) · [Real-or-complex lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib3/commit/19beb1274431d951ebc385fc72ebe9e78611c4bf) · [Semilinear lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/e02195e618334c2758d6091507d0342274dc8113)
- **Sébastien Gouëzel** introduced the Fourier inversion proof. **Jack Valmadre** introduced the Schwartz-to-$L^p$ continuous linear map. [Fourier inversion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/9fb833b8330ac5403dde5d09f5fb5bc49a40d220) · [Schwartz map to Lp](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/b9c7233cfdbab76db1cf230182a5e4447e081e90)

Mathlib is pinned in A2 to `0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474`. Johannes Hölzl and Kim Morrison's `Finsupp.Basic` supplies the pushforward and injectivity under an embedding. Its inverse identities on the image support are `comapDomain_add_of_injective` by Damiano Testa, `comapDomain_mapDomain` by Junyan Xu, and the ported `mapDomain_comapDomain`. `Finsupp.degree_mapDomain` in `Finsupp.Weight`, a file by Antoine Chambert-Loir and María Inés de Frutos-Fernández, proves degree preservation by summing every exponent, including for a map with collisions. Noah Walker introduced this hypothesis-free form, generalizing Bingyu Xia's `degree_mapDomain_eq_of_subsingletonAddUnits`. [Pushforward](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Basic.lean#L269-L320) · [Support and injectivity](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Basic.lean#L369-L439) · [Inverse](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Basic.lean#L597-L627) · [Degree](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Weight.lean#L274-L278) · [Comap addition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib3/commit/0c26348e2a26d8b22f0aa4402ffbcf1a33071af7) · [Comap inverse](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/2e77c8da6dc38a0304037c3e1f42e403ee4c1c0b) · [Degree with collisions](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/76ee00a560e037854d0b1779c0523fa1ec650927) · [Earlier degree form](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/commit/a19d30d2f7728f57bb9e93575df5012d096ccfbb)

Johan Commelin and Kenny Lau's `MvPowerSeries.Basic` gives convolution over the finite exponent antidiagonal. Chambert-Loir and de Frutos-Fernández's `MvPowerSeries.Substitution` identifies diagonal rescaling with formal substitution using zero constant terms. Riccardo Brasca and Bingyu Xia's `MvPowerSeries.Rename` gives the parallel classical restriction `killCompl` for an embedding and the forward rename with finite fibres. A2 proves the restriction product directly and uses it for the class witness and the original place controls. [Convolution](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/Basic.lean#L215-L223) · [Rescale coefficient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/Substitution.lean#L674-L676) · [Substitution](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/Substitution.lean#L737-L750) · [Restriction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/Rename.lean#L211-L250) · [Forward rename](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/Rename.lean#L109-L142)

The following fixed Mathlib sources were retrieved and checked against the original manuscript snapshots on 2026-11-28. The finite-dimension result supplies the promotion on the complete scalar field $\mathbb C$ with Hausdorff finite-dimensional domain. The Bochner result supplies evaluation of the already integrable kernel and commutation with the two bounded isometries. Joint composition and its preimage lemma apply to $L^2$ and real Borel Lebesgue measure, with compact-open continuous measure-preserving translations and finite-measure sets in the preimage argument.

- [FiniteDimension.lean:235–311](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/FiniteDimension.lean#L235-L311) · [ContinuousLinearMap.lean:44–81](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/ContinuousLinearMap.lean#L44-L81)
- [ContinuousPreimage.lean:49–96](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/ContinuousPreimage.lean#L49-L96) · [ContinuousCompMeasurePreserving.lean:42–106](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSpace/ContinuousCompMeasurePreserving.lean#L42-L106)

Masullo starts with a nonempty closed interval and takes a supremum over compact subintervals. Each term in the Hardy–Sobolev norm weights the two subinterval endpoints. The A2 cut $I_{a,b}$ in the kernel-vector module is a finite real-space cutoff. [Masullo, Definition 9.2.2.9, p. 416](https://math216.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/the-music-of-the-primes.pdf#page=416)

Bosch, Güntzer and Remmert, *Non-Archimedean Analysis* (1984), §3.1.2 Proposition 1, §3.2.1 Theorem 2 and Lemma 3, §3.2.4 Theorem 2 (pp. 129–130, 134–135, 139–140), give the spectral value, conjugate maximum, and complete-base valuation extension with finite-extension completeness. The operator and fixed-element smoothing are in §1.2.1 Proposition 2 and §1.3.2 Propositions 1–2. Sutherland, *Number Theory I*, Lecture 10, Proposition 10.3, Theorem 10.4 and Remark 10.7, specializes to finite extensions of the fraction field of a complete DVR. Serre, *Local Fields*, Ch. II §1 Proposition 1, gives the locally compact complete discrete case with finite residue field. Milne, *Algebraic Number Theory* v3.08, Theorem 7.38, Remark 7.41 and Proposition 7.46, records that discrete specialization, the infinite algebraic boundary, and compactness of the unit ball. The local-field theorem is classical. The archive-specific reading identifies the norm and topology on the finite fixed field. With base Dedekind ring $\mathbb Z$, fraction field $\mathbb Q$, finite field extension $K$, and integral closure $\mathcal O_K$, the proposition gives integral trace. The theorem gives perfect field trace duality for the finite separable extension, with a multiplication-by-inverse argument in its field proof. A2 takes the trace-nonzero test element to be $1$ in characteristic zero. Lecture 6, §6.5 p. 8 gives the integral basis and its rational-basis property. Lecture 5 PDF SHA-256 `e39bac6835a215fcb5172acbf01b628c1026de013d6ba647b109030556f1e43f` and Lecture 6 PDF SHA-256 `d3cdd31dee6af24dee052a8051eab1aa0bf6cb6c515b82d3aa152aa5b5044576`. - Oliver Braun and Renaud Coulangeon, author preprint arXiv:1304.0559v1 (2 April 2013), §4.1, Definition 4.11 and Theorem 4.12, p. 12, with the automorphism use on p. 14. The source assumes an imaginary quadratic field, two nondegenerate Hermitian forms and preservation of both field trace tests on every pair by a rational-linear map. It uses the ordinary trace and the trace of a generator times the form value, and identifies the resulting map as field-linear preserving the form. In our two models, positivity gives nondegeneracy, our common rational frames extend the entrywise equations to all pairs, $i$ is a quadratic generator, and the twist is $\operatorname{Tr}(-i h)$ by our first-argument convention. Their trace-form normalization by $1/2$ does not change equality of the tests. This covers the quadratic specializations as classical exposition. Their theorem is itself presented as known. The closed claim is any assertion of novelty for this trace comparison or the quadratic example mechanism. The general-field source proof, reconstruction from real independence and finite-code handoff are credited to A2 as formal production. The textbook proof, examples, counterexample and line-by-line use map are the book's contribution. SHA-256 `241017415705e84e242c25cb092dd19aa0cc0762657d70094b7c4530eafa8c46`. ### Chapter 2 §2.3.2.7.7 — Hilbert projection and conditional expectation

- **François Clément and Vincent Martin,** *The Lax–Milgram Theorem. A detailed proof to be formalized in Coq*, Inria RR-8934 (2016), §4.5.1, Theorem 180 and Lemma 181, pp. 46–48. The real nonempty complete convex set and the segment criterion give the written projection antecedent cited by Mathlib. [Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.03618)
- **A. N. Kolmogorov,** *Foundations of the Theory of Probability*, Chapter V, §4, pp. 52–53 in the English translation. The probability-space integral test on the induced measurable space and uniqueness up to equivalence are the classical model for the function-level comparison. [English translation](https://liyingli-math.github.io/teaching/notes/Kolmogorov1933.pdf)
- **Steven P. Lalley,** *Conditional Expectation*, §1, Definition 1, Exercise 2 and properties (0)–(4), pp. 1–2. The real probability-space projection gives the finite-partition means, best prediction and covariance tests. [Author's notes](https://galton.uchicago.edu/~lalley/Courses/383/ConditionalExpectation.pdf)
- **Mathlib M0 [Lean, read].** The pin is `0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474`. The real minimizer and real/complex tests feed the projection instance. The complement API forms the linear first coordinate and packages its continuity. The subspace `lpMeas` inherits completeness on the trim and the Hilbert map feeds `condExpL2` without a $\sigma$-finite assumption. Finite-set integration and the later integrable comparison have the distinct hypotheses given in the section. [Minimizers](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Projection/Minimal.lean#L34-L307) · [Projection](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Projection/Basic.lean#L47-L125) · [Linear assembly](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Projection.lean#L76-L127) · [Continuous assembly](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/Complement.lean#L154-L166) · [Measurable subspace](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation/AEMeasurable.lean#L264-L312) · [L² projection and tests](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation/CondexpL2.lean#L67-L252) · [Comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation/Basic.lean#L386-L401)
